body:
Is `DSM` linux based? I'm guessing so.

I think it is unlikely that this is a problem with DSM or rclone running on DSM, I think it is more likely a problem with the environment being different somehow.  Some ideas at random: perhaps the IP of the DSM got blacklisted by Google and the one on your laptop wasn't or maybe one uses IPv4 and one IPv6, or maybe they use different resolvers and so are hitting different endpoints, or maybe the round robin dns gave them different endpoints...

> 2019/06/26 18:10:09 ERROR : xxxx/xxxx (2018)/xxxxx - 01x01 - Piloto.mkv: Failed to copy: googleapi: Error 500: Internal Error, internalError

There have been reports of other people gettng that error https://github.com/ncw/rclone/issues/3155 and https://github.com/ncw/rclone/issues/3070 which I haven't got to the bottom of.

There shouldn't be any secrets in the debug, but there may be names of files etc which you want to keep secret.  Feel free to edit the debug before posting.

Here is... if I have to something else, please.. let me know
[backup.txt.zip](https://github.com/ncw/rclone/files/3346808/backup.txt.zip)

I can see these errors in the logs

```
  68945:2019/07/01 19:47:59 DEBUG : pacer: low level retry 1/3 (error googleapi: Error 500: Internal Error, internalError)
  91791:2019/07/01 19:49:31 DEBUG : pacer: low level retry 2/3 (error googleapi: Error 500: Internal Error, internalError)
  91839:2019/07/01 19:51:00 DEBUG : pacer: low level retry 3/3 (error googleapi: Error 500: Internal Error, internalError)
  91906:2019/07/01 19:52:33 DEBUG : pacer: low level retry 1/3 (error googleapi: Error 503: Backend Error, backendError)
```

As far as I can see the request looks OK

```
2019/07/01 19:46:30 DEBUG : HTTP REQUEST (req 0xc000958700)
2019/07/01 19:46:30 DEBUG : POST /drive/v3/files/17mEOBIWgq2j-RcmVaoUbwdJzJ0KlOd7M/copy?alt=json&fields=id%2Cname%2Csize%2Cmd5Checksum%2Ctrashed%2CmodifiedTime%2CcreatedTime%2CmimeType%2Cparents%2CwebViewLink&keepRevisionForever=false&prettyPrint=false&supportsTeamDrives=false HTTP/1.1

Content-Length: 211
Authorization: XXXX
Content-Type: application/json
Accept-Encoding: gzip
```

It is just that google didn't want to complete the action.  It took 90s thinking about it so maybe it was an internal timeout or something like that.

```
2019/07/01 19:47:59 DEBUG : HTTP RESPONSE (req 0xc000958700)

Transfer-Encoding: chunked
Alt-Svc: quic=":443"; ma=2592000; v="46,44,43,39"
```

So I still think this is some sort of problem at Google, but I don't know what.

The weird thing, is that only happens under DSM... :(
Well, maybe in a future version, will work
